sources.title: Kiribati Natural Disasters and Climate Change Survey Report 2023–2024
sources.organization: Kiribati National Statistics Office and Pacific Community
sources.temporal_coverage: Household impacts during 2023–2024; HIES survey period.
sources.methodology: Natural-disaster module in the 2023–2024 Household Income and Expenditure Survey; 1,208 households interviewed, weighted for population estimates.
sources.limitations: PDF is marked DRAFT. Results have sampling uncertainty, no cross-variable statistical correlations, and an internal 25%/26% affected-population discrepancy; affected-household results are used instead.

sources.title: Third National Communication of the Republic of Kiribati to the UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Kiribati, Ministry of Environment, Lands and Agricultural Development
sources.temporal_coverage: National circumstances and impacts through the report's March 2025 version; some drought history is retrospective.
sources.methodology: Government NC3 consolidating sector reports and climate-risk tables; cited passages concern coastal relocation, freshwater and land disputes.
sources.limitations: PDF is draft-marked despite its foreword's statement of Cabinet approval; cited tables give no dates for the risk statements.

sources.title: Enhancing a Whole-of-Islands Approach to Strengthen Community Resilience to Climate and Disaster Risks in Kiribati
geographic_coverage: Five pilot islands, not named on the consulted page
sources.methodology: UNDP project-page summary of programme objectives, target beneficiaries and planned components.
sources.limitations: Targets and activities are planned benefits, not evaluated outcomes; the page does not name the five pilot islands.

sources.title: Early Warning and Early Action in Kiribati
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, Sub-Regional Office for the Pacific
sources.temporal_coverage: Publication page describes current early-warning initiatives in 2025.
sources.methodology: Publisher summary of a four-page country brief on Early Warnings for All and Weather Ready Pacific initiatives.
sources.limitations: The linked PDF was not readable in the web reader; claims are limited to the publisher's official summary, which gives no island-level coverage or outcome measures.

claims.locator: Printed p. vi, key results; printed pp. 8–9, Table 5
claims.paraphrase: The 2023–2024 survey estimates that one quarter of households were impacted by natural disasters; strong winds were most often reported, followed by heavy rain, extreme temperatures, sea-water rise and drought.
claims.limitations: Household survey estimates have sampling uncertainty; the report's key summary gives a different population share.

claims.locator: Printed p. vi, key results; printed pp. 11–12, Table 7; p. 15, Table 9
claims.paraphrase: Among surveyed farming households reporting disaster-related agricultural losses, drought was cited by 47%; dwelling damage affected 60% of disaster-affected households, while drought disrupted water service for 21% of households reporting basic-service disruption.
claims.limitations: Denominators differ by table and result; percentages describe reported impacts, not causal estimates.

claims.locator: Printed p. 100, Table 4.6, freshwater and sanitation: observed/potential climate impacts
claims.paraphrase: Past droughts in South Tarawa and Banaba caused acute freshwater shortages, well salinity and temporary island abandonment.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Lands and Agricultural Development
claims.limitations: No episode dates or household counts are given.

claims.locator: Printed p. 99, Table 4.5, coastal infrastructure and transport impacts
claims.paraphrase: The NC3 identifies potential landowner–landowner disputes and land-demarcation conflict with government if private buildings or public infrastructure must be relocated amid climate-related coastal impacts.
claims.scenario: Source-unspecified; relocation horizon is not stated.
geographies: Kiribati coastal communities; South Tarawa and outer islands are named in the surrounding table
claims.limitations: Conditional warning, not observed climate-caused disputes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-related relocation may increase landowner and government demarcation disputes.

claims.locator: Printed p. 100, Table 4.6, water-reserve conflict and impacts
claims.paraphrase: NC3 reports tensions over reserves declared on private land, costly disputes and vandalism; it separately names South Tarawa, Banaba and Tabakea for reserve encroachment.
claims.limitations: Current disputes are not attributed to climate change.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Reserve declarations on private land lead to tensions, disputes and vandalism of water infrastructure.

claims.locator: Project summary and Impact fields; project date and status
claims.paraphrase: UNDP lists an ongoing whole-of-islands programme targeting five pilot islands and 17,500 people (49% women), with planned island-level climate-resilient planning and water, food-security and infrastructure measures.
geographies: Five pilot islands, unnamed on the page
claims.limitations: The programme is ongoing; 17,500 and 49% women are targets, not verified beneficiaries or outcomes.

claims.locator: Project summary, barriers and four components
claims.paraphrase: UNDP identifies institutional and technical barriers to adaptation and lists stronger policies, island-level planning, knowledge and communication as programme components.
geographies: Kiribati national; five pilot islands, unnamed
claims.limitations: The page describes the programme rationale and planned components, not an independent capacity assessment or completed results.

claims.locator: Official publication-page summary, paragraphs on remote islands and approaches
claims.paraphrase: UNDRR's 2025 brief describes satellite connectivity and drought anticipatory action as helping Kiribati communicate timely warnings to remote-island communities.
claims.limitations: Based on publisher summary only; the brief's full text and local coverage measures were inaccessible in the reader.

access_audit.reuse_terms: Partial scientific/educational/research reproduction authorized with attribution; no long text copied.

access_audit.reuse_terms: No reuse terms reviewed; paraphrased only.

search_audit.query: Kiribati 2023 2024 natural disaster household survey drought water agriculture regional results government report
search_audit.outcome: Found a recent national survey with household-level impacts and an NC3 naming South Tarawa, Banaba and Tabakea; the survey PDF is draft-marked and lacks island-level breakdowns.

search_audit.query: Kiribati climate relocation land ownership disputes conflict government landowners UNFCCC
search_audit.outcome: Found the NC3's explicit conditional warning that climate-related relocation may increase landowner and government demarcation disputes; no scenario or timing is stated.

search_audit.query: Kiribati water reserve private land disputes vandalism groundwater borehole conflict South Tarawa climate
search_audit.outcome: The NC3 links reserve declarations to community-government disputes and vandalism of water infrastructure and monitoring; it does not attribute current disputes to climate change.

search_audit.query: Kiribati outer islands resilience early warning satellite drought anticipatory action UNDP UNDRR
search_audit.outcome: Found an ongoing UNDP programme with planned whole-island capacity and adaptation components and an UNDRR publisher summary of satellite-enabled warnings; output status and access limits are reported.

gaps: The 2023–2024 household survey reports national results, not island-level exposure; total affected population differs between its key-results page and detailed text, so no population-wide total is used.
The government NC3 remains visibly draft-marked and gives no scenario or time horizon for relocation-related disputes; current water-reserve conflict is not attributed to climate change.
No accessible primary evidence in this search measured the prevalence of climate-related conflict or the outcomes of whole-of-islands and early-warning interventions.
